  'sewer-repair-cost-london-ontario',
  'How Much Does Sewer Repair Cost in London Ontario?',
  'Sewer repair costs in London Ontario vary widely depending on the method used, the depth of the pipe, and the extent of the damage. Here is what you can expect to pay and why.',
  'Sewer repair is one of the more significant home expenses a London Ontario homeowner can face. The range is wide, and the variation is real. A simple drain cleaning might cost a few hundred dollars. A full sewer line replacement with open-cut excavation can run into the tens of thousands. Understanding what drives the cost helps you evaluate quotes and avoid overpaying.

## What Affects the Cost of Sewer Repair in London Ontario

The single biggest factor is the repair method. There are four main approaches used in London Ontario, and each has a different cost profile.

**Open-cut excavation** is the traditional approach. The crew digs a trench to expose the damaged section, replaces the pipe, and restores the surface. It is the most disruptive method but sometimes the only option for severely collapsed pipes or deep installations. Costs typically range from $5,000 to $20,000 or more depending on depth, length, and surface materials.

**UV-cured CIPP lining** (Cured-In-Place Pipe) is a trenchless method that inserts a resin-saturated liner into the existing pipe and cures it in place using UV light. The result is a new pipe inside the old one, with no excavation required. For a standard residential sewer line in London, this typically costs between $3,500 and $8,000 depending on pipe diameter and length.

**Pipe bursting** is another trenchless option where a bursting head fractures the old pipe outward while pulling a new pipe through in its place. It requires access pits at each end but no open trench. Costs are similar to CIPP lining.

**Spot patch repair** using systems like PipePatch addresses localized damage without lining the full length of the pipe. For a single damaged joint or short section, this can cost $1,500 to $3,500.

## The London Ontario PDC Program

Homeowners in London Ontario who need to replace the private drain connection (the section of sewer line between the house and the city main) may qualify for the Private Drain Connection (PDC) Renewal Program. The program offers a flat-rate replacement at $7,250 plus HST for qualifying properties. This is significantly less than the open market cost for the same work and is worth checking before accepting any quote.

Discount Drain participates in the PDC program and can advise you on whether your property qualifies.

## What a Sewer Repair Quote Should Include

A legitimate sewer repair quote should always start with a camera inspection. Any company that quotes a price without first inspecting the pipe is guessing. At Discount Drain, the camera inspection is free and included with every service call. You watch the footage on site so you understand exactly what is wrong before any work begins.

The quote should specify the repair method, the length of pipe being addressed, what surface restoration is included, and the warranty on the work. Be cautious of quotes that are vague on method or that exclude surface restoration.

## Common Sewer Problems in London Ontario

London has a large stock of older housing, particularly in the Old North, Byron, and Old South neighbourhoods. Many of these homes have original clay tile sewer lines that are 50 to 80 years old. Clay tile is susceptible to root intrusion at the joints and can crack or collapse as the soil shifts over time.

Cast iron drain lines inside older homes are also common and can corrode from the inside, reducing flow capacity and eventually failing. The ElastoFlake spray coating system can rehabilitate cast iron pipes from the inside without replacement.

## Getting an Honest Assessment

The best way to get an accurate cost estimate is to call for a free camera inspection. The footage tells you exactly what you are dealing with, and a reputable company will walk you through the options and explain the tradeoffs between methods honestly.

Discount Drain has been doing sewer repair in London Ontario since 1970. We will show you the camera footage, explain your options, and give you a written quote before any work begins. Call 519-451-8342 or request a free quote online.',

  'Honest breakdown of sewer repair costs in London Ontario. Learn what affects the price, what to expect from a quote, and how to avoid overpaying.',

  'wet-basement-fix-london-ontario',
  'How to Fix a Wet Basement in London Ontario: What Actually Works',
  'A wet basement in London Ontario is rarely just a cosmetic problem. Understanding the source of the water is the first step to fixing it permanently.',
  'Wet basements are one of the most common calls we receive at Discount Drain, particularly in spring when snowmelt and rain put maximum pressure on foundations across London Ontario. The good news is that most wet basement problems are fixable. The key is identifying the actual source of the water before spending money on a solution.

## Why London Ontario Basements Get Wet

London sits on clay-heavy soil that does not drain well. When it rains heavily or snow melts quickly, water accumulates around foundations faster than the soil can absorb it. This hydrostatic pressure pushes water through any available path: cracks in poured concrete walls, gaps at the floor-wall joint, deteriorated window wells, and failed weeping tile.

Weeping tile is the perforated pipe buried around the perimeter of the foundation that is supposed to collect groundwater and direct it to a sump pit or storm sewer. In homes built before the 1980s, this is often clay tile that has collapsed, become clogged with roots, or simply failed after decades of use. When the weeping tile stops working, water has nowhere to go except into the basement.

## The Four Main Wet Basement Solutions

**Interior drainage system with sump pump.** A perimeter channel is cut into the basement floor along the walls, a drainage pipe is installed, and a sump pit and pump are added to remove the collected water. This does not stop water from entering the wall but intercepts it before it reaches the floor. A battery backup sump pump is essential for power outages during storms. This is the most common solution for moderate water intrusion and typically costs $3,000 to $8,000 depending on the perimeter length.

**Exterior waterproofing.** The foundation is excavated from the outside, a waterproof membrane is applied to the wall, and new weeping tile is installed. This stops water at the source rather than managing it after entry. It is more disruptive and more expensive ($8,000 to $20,000 for a full perimeter), but it is the most thorough solution for severe or chronic water problems. Discount Drain backs exterior waterproofing work with a 20-year written warranty.

**Crack injection.** Structural cracks in poured concrete walls are sealed from the inside using epoxy or polyurethane injection. This is appropriate for isolated cracks that are the primary entry point. It is less expensive than full waterproofing but only addresses the specific crack, not the underlying drainage problem.

**Sewer camera inspection first.** Before any waterproofing work begins, it is worth checking whether a blocked or broken weeping tile connection to the sewer is contributing to the problem. A free camera inspection can rule that out and prevent spending money on waterproofing when the real issue is a drainage blockage.

## What the 20-Year Warranty Covers

Discount Drain''s 20-year warranty on wet basement work covers water re-entry in the repaired area. If water returns through the same path we addressed within 20 years, we come back and fix it at no charge. The warranty transfers to new owners if you sell the property, which can be a meaningful selling point.

The warranty does not cover new cracks that develop in different locations or water entry through paths that were not part of the original repair scope. We are clear about this upfront.

## What Does Not Work Long Term

Painting the interior walls with hydraulic cement or waterproof paint addresses the symptom but not the cause. These products slow water entry temporarily but do not stop hydrostatic pressure. They are not a substitute for proper drainage.

Regrading the soil around the foundation to slope away from the house is a useful supplement to proper drainage but rarely sufficient on its own for a chronic wet basement problem.

## Getting a Proper Assessment

The right solution depends on where the water is coming from, how much water is entering, and the condition of the existing drainage system. A proper assessment starts with a camera inspection of the weeping tile and sewer connection, followed by an inspection of the foundation walls and floor.

Call Discount Drain at 519-451-8342 for a free assessment. We have been fixing wet basements in London Ontario since 1970 and can tell you honestly which solution makes sense for your specific situation.',

  'trenchless-vs-excavation-sewer-repair',
  'Trenchless Sewer Repair vs. Excavation: Which One Is Right for You?',
  'Trenchless sewer repair sounds appealing, but it is not always the right choice. Here is an honest comparison of trenchless and excavation methods for London Ontario homeowners.',
  'The phrase "no-dig sewer repair" has become a popular selling point in the drain industry, and for good reason. Trenchless methods genuinely do save homeowners from having their driveways torn up in many cases. But trenchless is not always the right answer, and a contractor who recommends it for every job is not giving you an honest assessment.

Here is how to think about the choice between trenchless repair and traditional excavation.

## What Trenchless Repair Actually Means

Trenchless is an umbrella term for several methods that repair or replace underground pipe without open-cut excavation. The three main methods used in London Ontario are:

**UV-cured CIPP lining.** A flexible liner saturated with resin is pulled into the existing pipe and inflated against the pipe wall. UV light cures the resin, creating a new pipe inside the old one. The liner is seamless, with no joints for roots to enter. This method works well for pipes with cracks, root intrusion, or corrosion where the pipe still has structural integrity.

**Pipe bursting.** A bursting head is pulled through the old pipe, fracturing it outward while simultaneously pulling a new pipe through in its place. This replaces the pipe entirely rather than lining it. It requires access pits at each end but no open trench along the pipe run. It is a good option when the existing pipe is too damaged to line.

**Spot patch repair.** For localized damage at a single joint or short section, a spot patch using silicate epoxy resin can repair the specific area without lining the full pipe. This is faster and less expensive than full-length lining when the damage is contained.

## When Trenchless Is the Right Choice

Trenchless lining is well-suited to situations where the pipe has cracks, root intrusion, or corrosion but still has enough structural integrity to support the liner during installation. It is particularly valuable when the pipe runs under a driveway, patio, finished landscaping, or a structure that would be expensive to restore after excavation.

For most residential sewer lines in London Ontario that show root intrusion or cracking on camera inspection, trenchless lining is a reasonable first option to evaluate.

## When Excavation Is Necessary

Trenchless methods have limitations. A pipe that has collapsed, offset significantly at a joint, or been crushed by root pressure or soil movement may not be a candidate for lining. If the camera shows that the pipe has lost its round shape or has sections that are completely blocked, lining may not be possible.

Excavation is also the right choice when the pipe needs to be repositioned, when the grade (slope) of the pipe needs to be corrected, or when the pipe material is incompatible with lining systems.

For pipes that run through open lawn with no expensive surface materials above them, excavation may also be the more cost-effective option, particularly for longer runs.

## The Honest Answer

The right method depends on what the camera shows. A contractor who recommends trenchless before inspecting the pipe is guessing. A contractor who always recommends excavation regardless of what the camera shows may be steering you toward a more expensive job.

At Discount Drain, every job starts with a free camera inspection. We show you the footage on site and explain what we found. If trenchless is appropriate, we will tell you. If excavation is necessary, we will explain why. We use all three trenchless methods as well as traditional excavation, so we have no financial incentive to push one approach over another.

Call 519-451-8342 to book a free camera inspection. We serve London and all of Southwestern Ontario.',

  'how-often-drain-cleaning-london-ontario',
  'How Often Should You Have Your Drains Cleaned in London Ontario?',
  'Most London Ontario homeowners wait until a drain is completely blocked before calling. Here is a smarter approach to drain maintenance.',
  'Most homeowners only think about their drains when something goes wrong. A slow kitchen sink, a gurgling toilet, or water backing up in the basement floor drain are the usual triggers for a service call. By that point, the blockage has usually been building for months.

A more practical approach is to think about drain cleaning the way you think about furnace maintenance: something you schedule before there is a problem, not after.

## How Often for a Typical London Ontario Home

For a single-family home with no history of drain problems and no large trees near the sewer line, a camera inspection and drain cleaning every three to five years is a reasonable maintenance interval. This catches root intrusion and grease buildup before they cause a backup.

For older homes in London''s established neighbourhoods, particularly those with mature trees and original clay tile sewer lines, annual or biennial inspection is worth considering. Clay tile sewer lines have joints every few feet, and each joint is a potential entry point for tree roots. Once roots establish themselves in a line, they grow back faster each year.

## Kitchen Drains

Kitchen drains accumulate grease and food debris regardless of how careful you are. Grease cools and solidifies on the inside of drain pipes, gradually narrowing the flow path. In a busy kitchen, a professional cleaning every one to two years prevents the kind of complete blockage that shuts down the sink.

Restaurants and commercial kitchens should be on a more frequent schedule, typically quarterly or monthly depending on volume.

## Bathroom Drains

Bathroom drains collect hair, soap scum, and toothpaste residue. Most bathroom drain blockages are in the trap or the first few feet of pipe and can be cleared with a drain snake. If multiple bathroom drains are slow at the same time, the problem is usually further down the line in the main stack or sewer connection.

## Signs You Should Not Wait

Some signs indicate a drain problem that should be addressed promptly rather than scheduled for routine maintenance:

Multiple drains slowing at the same time suggests a blockage in the main sewer line rather than an individual drain. This can escalate to a sewage backup quickly.

Gurgling sounds from drains or the toilet when water drains elsewhere in the house indicates air being pushed back through the system, which is a sign of a partial blockage in the main line.

Water backing up into the basement floor drain is a serious warning sign. The floor drain is the lowest point in the drain system, so it is the first place sewage appears when the main line is blocked.

A sewage smell in the basement without visible water can indicate a dry trap (pour water into floor drains periodically) or a cracked sewer line.

## The Value of a Camera Inspection

A camera inspection before drain cleaning tells you what you are dealing with. If the line has root intrusion, a simple cleaning will clear it temporarily but the roots will return. Knowing that root intrusion is present lets you make an informed decision about whether to schedule regular maintenance cleanings or address the root cause with a trenchless repair.

Discount Drain includes a free camera inspection with every service call. Call 519-451-8342 to schedule a drain cleaning and inspection in London Ontario.',
  'How Often Should You Clean Drains London Ontario | Discount Drain',
  'Drain cleaning frequency depends on your home, your trees, and your habits. Here is a practical guide for London Ontario homeowners.',

  'pre-purchase-sewer-inspection-london-ontario',
  'Why You Need a Sewer Inspection Before Buying a Home in London Ontario',
  'A standard home inspection does not cover the sewer line. Here is why a pre-purchase sewer camera inspection is one of the smartest things a London Ontario home buyer can do.',
  'Buying a home in London Ontario is one of the largest financial decisions most people make. A standard home inspection covers the visible and accessible components of the property: the roof, the electrical panel, the furnace, the windows. What it does not cover is the sewer line running from the house to the city main underground.

For many London Ontario homes, particularly those built before 1980, the sewer line is one of the most significant deferred maintenance items on the property. And because it is underground, it is invisible until it fails.

## What a Standard Home Inspection Misses

A licensed home inspector in Ontario is not required to inspect the sewer line as part of a standard inspection. Most inspectors will note the age of the home and flag that older homes may have clay tile sewer lines, but they cannot tell you the condition of the pipe without a camera inspection.

Clay tile sewer lines were the standard in London Ontario until the 1960s and 1970s when plastic pipe became common. Clay tile has a lifespan of 50 to 100 years under good conditions, but root intrusion, soil movement, and ground settling can cause failures much earlier. A home built in 1955 with an original clay tile sewer line may have a pipe that is functioning adequately today but is one heavy rainstorm or root intrusion event away from a backup.

## What a Camera Inspection Reveals

A sewer camera inspection pushes a high-resolution camera through the drain line from a cleanout access point, recording footage of the full length of the accessible pipe. The inspection can identify:

Root intrusion at clay tile joints, ranging from fine root hairs to full root masses that are partially or completely blocking the pipe.

Cracks, fractures, or offset joints where sections of pipe have shifted relative to each other.

Corrosion or buildup inside cast iron pipes that reduces flow capacity.

Collapsed sections where the pipe has lost its structural integrity.

The location of the connection to the city main, which helps determine whether any problems are on the private side (the homeowner''s responsibility) or the city side.

## How Much Does a Pre-Purchase Inspection Cost

At Discount Drain, the camera inspection is free when combined with a service call. For a standalone pre-purchase inspection, the cost is typically $150 to $300 depending on the length and accessibility of the line. This is a small investment relative to the cost of a sewer line repair or replacement, which can range from $3,500 for a trenchless repair to $15,000 or more for full excavation and replacement.

## What to Do If Problems Are Found

If the camera inspection reveals root intrusion, cracks, or other issues, you have several options. You can negotiate a price reduction with the seller to account for the cost of repair. You can ask the seller to repair the line before closing. Or you can proceed with the purchase knowing what you are taking on and budget accordingly.

In some cases, the problems found are minor and can be managed with regular drain cleaning. In other cases, the inspection reveals a sewer line that needs immediate attention. Either way, you are making an informed decision rather than discovering the problem after you have moved in.

## Booking a Pre-Purchase Inspection

Discount Drain performs pre-purchase sewer inspections throughout London Ontario and Southwestern Ontario. We can typically schedule an inspection within one to two business days, which fits within most real estate transaction timelines.

Call 519-451-8342 or request an appointment online. We will provide a written report of our findings that you can use in your purchase negotiations.',
  'Pre-Purchase Sewer Inspection London Ontario | Discount Drain',
  'A standard home inspection does not include a sewer camera inspection. For older London homes, this is a significant gap that can cost buyers thousands after closing.',
  '/manus-storage/service-camera-inspection_dbb5bfc5.jpg',
  'sewer-camera',
  1,
  '2024-05-22 09:00:00'
);

## How Often for a Typical London Ontario Home

For a single-family home with no history of drain problems and no large trees near the sewer line, a camera inspection and drain cleaning every three to five years is a reasonable maintenance interval. This catches root intrusion and grease buildup before they cause a backup.

For older homes in London''s established neighbourhoods, particularly those with mature trees and original clay tile sewer lines, annual or biennial inspection is worth considering. Clay tile sewer lines have joints every few feet, and each joint is a potential entry point for tree roots. Once roots establish themselves in a line, they grow back faster each year.

## Kitchen Drains

Kitchen drains accumulate grease and food debris regardless of how careful you are. Grease cools and solidifies on the inside of drain pipes, gradually narrowing the flow path. In a busy kitchen, a professional cleaning every one to two years prevents the kind of complete blockage that shuts down the sink.

Restaurants and commercial kitchens should be on a more frequent schedule, typically quarterly or monthly depending on volume.

## Bathroom Drains

Bathroom drains collect hair, soap scum, and toothpaste residue. Most bathroom drain blockages are in the trap or the first few feet of pipe and can be cleared with a drain snake. If multiple bathroom drains are slow at the same time, the problem is usually further down the line in the main stack or sewer connection.

## Signs You Should Not Wait

Some signs indicate a drain problem that should be addressed promptly rather than scheduled for routine maintenance:

Multiple drains slowing at the same time suggests a blockage in the main sewer line rather than an individual drain. This can escalate to a sewage backup quickly.

Gurgling sounds from drains or the toilet when water drains elsewhere in the house indicates air being pushed back through the system, which is a sign of a partial blockage in the main line.

Water backing up into the basement floor drain is a serious warning sign. The floor drain is the lowest point in the drain system, so it is the first place sewage appears when the main line is blocked.

A sewage smell in the basement without visible water can indicate a dry trap (pour water into floor drains periodically) or a cracked sewer line.

  'Buying a home in London Ontario is one of the largest financial decisions most people make. A standard home inspection covers the visible and accessible components of the property: the roof, the electrical panel, the furnace, the windows. What it does not cover is the sewer line running from the house to the city main underground.

For many London Ontario homes, particularly those built before 1980, the sewer line is one of the most significant deferred maintenance items on the property. And because it is underground, it is invisible until it fails.

## What a Standard Home Inspection Misses

A licensed home inspector in Ontario is not required to inspect the sewer line as part of a standard inspection. Most inspectors will note the age of the home and flag that older homes may have clay tile sewer lines, but they cannot tell you the condition of the pipe without a camera inspection.

Clay tile sewer lines were the standard in London Ontario until the 1960s and 1970s when plastic pipe became common. Clay tile has a lifespan of 50 to 100 years under good conditions, but root intrusion, soil movement, and ground settling can cause failures much earlier. A home built in 1955 with an original clay tile sewer line may have a pipe that is functioning adequately today but is one heavy rainstorm or root intrusion event away from a backup.

## What a Camera Inspection Reveals

A sewer camera inspection pushes a high-resolution camera through the drain line from a cleanout access point, recording footage of the full length of the accessible pipe. The inspection can identify:

Root intrusion at clay tile joints, ranging from fine root hairs to full root masses that are partially or completely blocking the pipe.

Cracks, fractures, or offset joints where sections of pipe have shifted relative to each other.

Corrosion or buildup inside cast iron pipes that reduces flow capacity.

Collapsed sections where the pipe has lost its structural integrity.

The location of the connection to the city main, which helps determine whether any problems are on the private side (the homeowner''s responsibility) or the city side.

## How Much Does a Pre-Purchase Inspection Cost

At Discount Drain, the camera inspection is free when combined with a service call. For a standalone pre-purchase inspection, the cost is typically $150 to $300 depending on the length and accessibility of the line. This is a small investment relative to the cost of a sewer line repair or replacement, which can range from $3,500 for a trenchless repair to $15,000 or more for full excavation and replacement.

## What to Do If Problems Are Found

If the camera inspection reveals root intrusion, cracks, or other issues, you have several options. You can negotiate a price reduction with the seller to account for the cost of repair. You can ask the seller to repair the line before closing. Or you can proceed with the purchase knowing what you are taking on and budget accordingly.

In some cases, the problems found are minor and can be managed with regular drain cleaning. In other cases, the inspection reveals a sewer line that needs immediate attention. Either way, you are making an informed decision rather than discovering the problem after you have moved in.
